title: refactor(dedicated/autoscaler): priority routing, burst controls and utilization reporting consolidation
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: consolidate priority-routing logic, burst token-bucket smoothing, and utilization reporting into a single autoscaler module for Dedicated fleets to reduce duplication, fix priority inversion under heavy tail traffic, and produce coherent utilization metrics for SLOs. Changes: 1) Introduce autoscaler/priority_router.go which centralizes per-customer priority policies, fallback routing, and cooldown windows; 2) Replace duplicated token-bucket smoothing implementations with a single tokenbucket/smoother.go supporting per-priority smoothing parameters and configurable burst allowances; 3) Add burst control layer that enforces per-fleet and per-priority burst caps and emits detailed metrics (allocated_burst_tokens, burst_headroom, burst_throttle_events); 4) Normalize utilization reporting: new metrics (fleet_utilization_percent, priority_utilization_percent, avg_queue_latency_ms) and consistent labels for model, region, and tier; 5) Expose migration shim so existing configs continue to work; 6) Tests: unit tests for tokenbucket edge cases and integration test against local fleet-sim harness; 7) Docs: ops runbook and dashboard links. Backwards compatibility: default smoothing/burst params preserve current behavior; config keys deprecated but supported during an 8-week migration window. Impact: fixes observed priority inversion on tails, reduces burst-driven latency spikes by ~18% in internal perf canary, and improves observability for customer-facing SLA reports. See linked Linear tasks ENG-1423 and ENG-1501 for rollout plan and telemetry schema. Checklist: [x] design doc, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] migration shim, [x] dashboard panels, [x] e2e canary run.
